entries.exactPassage: Here’s the tension: some of the people who shaped you are no longer in your life. Some have moved away. Some have died. Some you have lost touch with. The gratitude you feel toward them has nowhere to go. That is a particular kind of grief—the grief of unexpressed gratitude. The only remedy is to express it to someone else. Pass on what they gave you. The mentor you cannot thank can still be honored—by mentoring someone else. The teacher you cannot find can still be honored—by teaching what they taught you. The debt is not cancelled by their absence. It is transferred. Pay it forward. That is how gratitude becomes legacy.
entries.concern: Passing on a contribution is described as the only remedy for unexpressed gratitude and grief.

entries.exactPassage: Here’s the tension: this plan will change. Life will happen. The plan is not a cage. It is a launch pad. The operator does not launch once and stop. She launches continuously—adjusting, adapting, relaunching. The Life Launch Plan is not the end of the journey. It is the beginning of the next one. The plans you have built over five years are not achievements to frame. They are tools to use. The test is not whether the plan is beautiful. The test is whether you will use it—on tired days, on hard days, on days when everything in you wants to drift. The operator's final exam is not on paper. It is in life. And here is the final, deepest truth: the section you are avoiding is the section that will teach you the most. Face it. Not later. Now. That is where your growth is. That is where the launcher earns her title.
entries.concern: The section avoided is asserted to be the one that teaches most without considering access, information, privacy or safety.
entries.proposedWording: Invite a genuine question and suitable support rather than assign a motive or require distressing disclosure.
